title: Zero-Trust API Security & Cryptography (PYTH_175_S1 to PYTH_175_S8)

slides.title: Modern Cryptography with PyCA
slides.prompt: Secure Python applications require strong cryptographic primitives for encryption, hashing, and token signing.
slides.codeSnippet:
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

key = Fernet.generate_key()
f = Fernet(key)
token = f.encrypt(b'Secret Data')

slides.title: Symmetric Encryption with Fernet
slides.prompt: Fill in the method used to decrypt an encrypted token using a shared secret Fernet key.

slides.title: Argon2 Password Hashing
slides.prompt: Why is Argon2id preferred over MD5 or plain SHA-256 for secure password hashing?
options: It is memory-hard and time-configurable, rendering GPU rainbow table attacks ineffective
It generates shorter hash output strings for fast database storage
It allows original passwords to be decrypted back by administrators
It eliminates the need to salt password inputs
slides.correctAnswer: It is memory-hard and time-configurable, rendering GPU rainbow table attacks ineffective

slides.title: Asymmetric RSA Keys
slides.prompt: Fill in the cryptography module used for asymmetric key pairs and digital signatures.

slides.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion Attacks
slides.prompt: How do you prevent 'alg: none' JWT signature verification vulnerability exploits?
options: Explicitly enforce whitelist allowed algorithms (e.g., ['RS256']) in the decode function
By storing JWT tokens inside local storage cookies
By setting short expiration times on authorization header tokens
By encrypting the user ID parameter inside payload fields
slides.correctAnswer: Explicitly enforce whitelist allowed algorithms (e.g., ['RS256']) in the decode function

slides.title: Zero-Trust Security Principle
slides.prompt: Which principle defines the foundational policy of a Zero-Trust network architecture?
options: Never trust, always verify every incoming request and identity explicitly regardless of perimeter
Trust all internal traffic originating from behind local VPN firewalls
Disable token expiration checks inside internal microservices
Allow unrestricted database read access across private subnets
slides.correctAnswer: Never trust, always verify every incoming request and identity explicitly regardless of perimeter
